correctness.rationale: On the strict-Lax all-shock locus, each right-state block \(A_k=DF(u^{(k)})-s_kI\) is invertible because \(s_k\) lies strictly off the spectrum. The columns for the \(n-1\) intermediate states and the right endpoint form a square block lower-triangular submatrix with diagonal \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\), proving surjectivity of the full endpoint-parameterized derivative at every admissible zero. Parametric transversality then gives invertibility of \(D_x\mathcal J\) for almost every endpoint pair. The all-shock objective is \(C^1\) in the \(C^2\) flux Banach topology, so the implicit function theorem gives a unique nearby zero; strict hyperbolicity, Lax inequalities, nondegeneracy, containment, and speed order are open and therefore persist. No finite experiment is used and no existence claim is made for endpoints lacking an all-shock solution.

originality.rationale: The closest 2026 theorem assumes genuine nonlinearity and a global regular-manifold hypothesis. Its text separately observes that genuine nonlinearity is used only for rarefactions and that strict Lax shocks make the shock state blocks invertible, but it still proves genericity on all nondegenerate zeros and invokes the regular-manifold hypothesis there. Restricting parametric transversality to the open admissible all-shock locus removes the regular-manifold assumption as well; no checked source states this arbitrary-dimensional, almost-every-endpoint, flux-perturbation theorem under strict hyperbolicity alone. Older shock-only work differs either in dimension/framework or in the perturbations considered.
residual_risks: The 2026 source makes the two local ingredients conspicuous, so experts may regard the admissible-locus refinement as an implicit observation even though the weakened theorem is not stated.
The Kong 2003 full text was not lawfully accessible in the checked sources; its abstract indicates a different perturbation problem, but uninspected details could contain a closer comparison.

value.rationale: The result removes two global standing assumptions from a natural and important arbitrary-dimensional theory. It shows that the regular-manifold condition is needed in the published genericity proof to control non-admissible Hugoniot zeros, not the physical strict-Lax all-shock zeros themselves. This gives a clean robustness theorem for strong all-shock solutions of strictly hyperbolic systems, including non-genuinely-nonlinear regimes, while preserving perturbations of the flux rather than only initial data. The gain is structural rather than a routine parameter specialization.
